## Simple explanation

YAML is a text format for writing structured data and configuration in a
readable way, commonly using indentation to show nested values.

## Technical explanation

YAML supports mappings, sequences, scalars, and other features. Indentation
is syntactic, so spaces and nesting matter. Different YAML versions and
parser behaviors can affect values such as booleans and numbers; configuration
systems may impose their own schema and restrictions.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

AI projects often use YAML to configure training jobs, data pipelines,
deployment, and CI. A malformed or ambiguous configuration can change
behavior, so configurations should be validated and reviewed like code.

## How it works

A YAML parser converts the document into structured values. Applications
then validate those values against expected fields, types, and constraints
before using them.

## Practical example

A training configuration can specify a dataset path, batch size, learning
rate, and random seed. Validate required fields and record the exact
configuration alongside the resulting model artifact.

## Common misconceptions

- YAML is not merely JSON with different punctuation; its indentation and
  scalar rules can introduce subtle parsing errors.
- A syntactically valid YAML file may still be invalid for the application
  that consumes it.
